deep.reconstruction:
Page 20 of a 69-page file on pseudoline systems, written in 1981 or later. The file is interrupted on the next page by autobiographical notes in German.

Top of the page: four reference figures of small pseudoline arrangements.
- (1) Four lines in general position, labelled '4 (G4)' (or C4). This is the simple 4-arrangement, with 6 double points.
- (2) Five pseudolines in general position, labelled '(D5)'. This is the simple 5-arrangement.
- (3) Five pseudolines 'en position particulière'. The drawing shows one triple point, the rest double.
- (4) Six pseudolines 'en position particulière'. The drawing is a triangle with three concurrent cevians, with 4 marked triple points (three vertices and the centre). This is the complete quadrangle: the 6 lines joining 4 points in general position, with 4 triple points and 3 double (diagonal) points.

The heavily corrected text appears to state a structure result. Every arrangement of pseudolines that is not reduced to 4 pseudolines contains a sub-arrangement of one of the types (2), (3) or (4). This would exclude case (1), and presumably trivial pencils and near-pencils. The statement holds provided the arrangement is 'non spécial'. That word is defined in a hard-to-read clause: roughly, the intersection of two 2-cells is empty, a single vertex, or a common edge or face. So it is a regularity condition on the cell decomposition of the projective plane cut out by the pseudolines.

The NB refines this. If the arrangement contains neither (2) nor (3), it is either of type (4), or of a new type (5). Type (5) has 7 pseudolines, formed from a quadrilateral together with its diagonals. The small sketch shows solid and dashed lines and five or six marked multiple points. It is plausibly the complete quadrangle extended by a diagonal line, i.e. a near-maximal 'dense' arrangement in which every 5-subarrangement has at least two multiple points. The final words seem to say this case remains to be studied ('reste à être étudié'). A last sentence ('Si elle ne contient...') is crossed out.

In modern terms: a forbidden or unavoidable sub-arrangement theorem for (pseudo)line arrangements. Small arrangements avoiding the simple 5-arrangement and the 5-arrangement with one triple point are those in which every 5 lines carry at least two multiple points. These are essentially the complete quadrangle and a 7-line extension, close to the extremal/Sylvester–Gallai-type arrangements (e.g. Grünbaum's lists of simplicial arrangements A(6,1), A(7,1)). The purpose within the file is presumably to reduce questions about general pseudoline systems to a few small 'local' configurations, perhaps for an inductive or combinatorial-type argument on the cell structure.
errors: The statement as written cannot be literally true for all arrangements: pencils and near-pencils with at least 5 lines contain none of (2), (3), (4). The hypothesis 'non spéciales' must exclude them, but the definition on the page is too garbled to verify.

Type (5) is described as 7 pseudolines 'formé d'un quadrilatère et des deux diagonales'. A quadrilateral plus two diagonals gives only 6 lines, so either 'complete quadrilateral + 3 diagonals' or 'quadrangle + line(s)' is meant. The count is ambiguous and the case is explicitly left unfinished.
No proof is given; the classification is stated as an observation and the 7-line case is left 'to be studied'.

ideas.what: Catalogue of small pseudoline arrangements: simple 4- and 5-arrangements, the 5-arrangement with one triple point, and the complete quadrangle (6 lines, 4 triple points)
ideas.modern_name: small (simple / simplicial) arrangements of pseudolines; complete quadrangle A(6,1)
ideas.where_published: Pseudoline systems are not, to my knowledge, treated in his published texts; possibly alluded to among themes in Esquisse d'un programme (unsure)

ideas.what: Unavoidable sub-configurations: every (non-special) arrangement other than the 4-line one contains a 5-line simple arrangement, a 5-line arrangement with one triple point, or the complete quadrangle; otherwise it is a specific 7-line arrangement
ideas.modern_name: unavoidable/forbidden sub-arrangements; Ramsey-type and Sylvester–Gallai-type structure of dense arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: related results on ordinary points and simplicial arrangements by Kelly–Moser, Grünbaum, Csima–Sawyer; no exact match known

ideas.what: Notion of 'non-special' arrangement via intersection pattern of closed 2-cells (empty, a vertex, or an edge)
ideas.modern_name: regular CW-structure / 'nice' cell decomposition condition on the arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in the oriented-matroid literature (Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler)

missed.claim: A small classification of pseudoline arrangements avoiding the simple 5-arrangement and the 5-arrangement with one triple point: the result is either the complete quadrangle or a 7-line configuration (quadrilateral plus diagonals), the latter left 'to be studied'.
missed.quote: Si elle ne contient (2) ni (3), dans ce cas elle est du type (4), ou du type (5) de 7 ps. droites formé d'un quadrilatère et des deux diagonales
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean, checkable statement about arrangements where every 5 lines have at least two multiple points. It is easily verified with modern oriented-matroid enumeration, but appears to be just a lemma in Grothendieck's private program, likely subsumed by known lists of small arrangements.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary combinatorial classification of small pseudoline arrangements, largely within known territory (Grünbaum's catalogues, oriented matroids). Interesting mainly as documentation of Grothendieck's 1980s pseudoline project, not as a new result.
transcription_corrections: Figure (1) label is '(G4)' or possibly '(C4)'; the '4' beside it is the number of lines.
Figure (4) caption reads '6 en position particulière' (complete quadrangle with 4 triple points marked); its label is '(4)'.
Opening line likely reads: 'Tout arrangement de 1-dim. de ps. droites qui n'est pas réduit à 4 ps. droites (ce qui exclut le cas (1)) contient une des types de configurations (2), (3), (4)'.
'quand elles ne sont réalisées' likely 'quand elles ne sont pas réalisées'.
'dans l'intersection de V des arrangements' likely 'dans l'intersection de 2 [faces] des arrangements … est vide, réduite à un sommet, deux faces fermées ont au plus une arête fermée' or similar.
NB: 'Si elle ne contient ni (2) ni (3), dans ce cas elle est du type (4), ou du type (5) de 7 ps. droites formé d'un quadrilatère et des deux diagonales'.
'points d'être étudié' probably 'reste à être étudié' / 'mérite d'être étudié'.
A small inline sketch of the 7-line type (5), with dashed lines and marked multiple points, is not mentioned in the transcription.
